## 1137ac565856

**A2 — Reproduced sampler-domain shortcut plus two review-infrastructure gaps; audited source left unchanged.**  The audited generator is bound to SHA-256 `25eaead4df876be4fc5214d816201b10b0af2420fc9ffee543e614189976cf26` and declared rule hash `37464b163bd2`. Its current sampler/validator requires every frame to enclose the red marker and requires the frames to be strictly nested. That restriction makes the plausible shortcut “select the globally smallest frame” observationally identical to the intended “select the smallest frame that encloses the marker.”

The retained 15×15 counterexample contains an 11×11 enclosing frame, a 7×7 enclosing frame, and a separate unrelated 3×3 frame. Exact Racket execution correctly returns the 7×7 enclosing frame; the global-smallest rival returns the unrelated 3×3 frame. The outputs differ. The input deliberately fails the generator's current `self_check` (`red marker is not strictly inside frame color 4`, frames not strictly nested, negative frame gap), so this is **not** a canonical-valid counterexample under the present documented domain. It is a concrete domain question showing that the generated distribution cannot teach the containment predicate independently of global size. A repair should admit at least one non-enclosing smaller frame while preserving the canonical rule, or explicitly document that all frames enclose the marker and narrow the intended rule accordingly.

Two independent audit checks also fail: the task test hard-codes an invalid `Path.parents[...]` root and therefore fails before pytest in the portable runtime, and the strict semantic gate finds no declared semantic contract (`strict_canonical_like`, `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`, or `lesson_identifiable`). No patch was made to this audit-only target.
